subject: URGENT: runtime latency spike affecting HumbleCart — mitigation & customer note
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-08-18T15:02:00Z
Subject: [ALERT] p95 spike + throughput dip — gen-api / humblecart / us-west

Folks —

We saw a sustained p95 increase from ~180ms -> 1.1s and a correlated throughput drop (QPS down ~28%) for requests originating from HumbleCart (us-west) starting ~14:52 UTC. Spike coincides with a fanout increase (many short prompts) for their checkout predictions.

Initial findings:
- Kernel scheduling on the new runtime host family (n2-highcpu-optimized) shows higher KV GC frequency under many small concurrent sessions.
- KV cache evictions spike; cache miss rate jumped from 4% -> 32%.
- No OOMs; GPU utilization is stable but CPU-side stalls are increasing the end-to-end time.

Immediate mitigations attempted:
- Disabled aggressive prefetch on a small cohort (10% of their traffic) — minor improvement but not enough.
- Increased per-worker KV allocation on two nodes — helped p95 to ~600ms but throughput still ~15% below baseline.

Recommended short-term actions (priority):
1) Route HumbleCart traffic to the stable gen-api pool (older runtime kernel) as a fallback (can be done via routing policy) — estimate 20 min to validate and flip.
2) Temporarily reduce batching window for this customer to avoid fanout amplification (config change) — ~10 min to deploy.
3) Open RINF ticket for infra to investigate kernel scheduling patches and quantify broader risk.

Sharing p95 graph and a sample kv-eviction log as attachments.

Ben
SRE — Inference Operations

On 2028-08-18 15:14 UTC Stephanie Nguyen wrote:
> Karthik — can you confirm whether the routing fallback (older runtime kernel) will change model variant behavior in a way that could affect HumbleCart's output quality?

Short answer: low risk. The stable pool is running the same model weights and quantization profile; differences are kernel-level scheduling and a slightly more conservative KV allocation profile. For their workload (many short prompts, low context), the observable generation quality should be unchanged.

Technical notes:
- Root cause hypothesis: new kernel introduced a micro-regression in the KV cache eviction heuristic when session fanout > 200 concurrent short-lived sessions. This leads to higher cache churn and CPU stalls.
- Rollback path: routing them to the stable pool uses existing variant tag 'gen-v1-stable' — behaviorally equivalent for their prompt patterns.
- Risk: if we flip routing at peak, they may see transient token-latency variance during warm-up (~3–5 minutes).

Proposed plan + ETA:
A) Prepare routing rule and canary (10% traffic) — 12 minutes to push and observe metrics.
B) If canary looks good (p95 improvement and throughput stabilizes), escalate to 100% in 20 more minutes.
C) Post-change: keep monitoring for 60 minutes and capture smoke test prompts from HumbleCart to validate quality.

I'll start the routing rule change now; will reply with canary ID and metrics. If product wants a kernel patch this week, infra needs a prioritized ticket and 1–2 devs on it (estimate 2–3 days to test patch + global rollout).

—Karthik
Principal SW Eng (Runtime)

Subject: HumbleCart — brief update on observed latency and next steps (draft)

Amelia —

Wanted to loop you in quickly. We observed higher-than-normal response times for some of your gen-api requests in the us-west region this afternoon. Our SRE team has identified the cause as kernel-level scheduling interactions on a subset of host instances and has a mitigation plan in flight.

Planned immediate actions:
- Route your traffic to a stable runtime pool (low-risk, same model behavior) — expected impact: p95 reduced toward baseline within ~30 minutes.
- Reduce batching window temporarily to limit fanout amplification during the warm-up window.
- We'll run a short quality smoke test with a handful of your prompts after the switch and share results.

What to expect from us:
- We'll execute the routing canary now and update you within 30 minutes with observed p95 and throughput numbers.
- If we need to keep you on the fallback longer, we'll propose a brief credit for the impacted window — we'll confirm next steps if that becomes necessary.

We're really sorry for any disruption at peak. We know checkout latency matters and we'll prioritize stability over new runtime rollouts while we clean this up.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Lead — Key Partnerships
Redwood Inference
